title: France's household cultural and leisure spending has shifted toward services while books and durable goods lose share
source_unit: INSEE, Cultural, sports and leisure expenditure, annual national accounts data 2000-2025
geography: France; household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

observations.period: 2021-2025; composition of household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

denominator.unit: million euros of household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure in 2025; category composition denominator

cultural_services_share_2021.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

cultural_services_share_2022.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

cultural_services_share_2023.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

cultural_services_share_2024.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

cultural_services_share_2025.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

cultural_services_2025_value.unit: million euros; cinema, live shows, museums, audiovisual subscriptions, and photo development included

mechanism.value: The household cultural-leisure basket has reweighted toward recurring or accessed services, consistent with a service/platform economy, but the aggregate category cannot identify who consumes them or whether quantity, price, or quality changed

observations.method: INSEE annual national accounts, base 2020, using the current COICOP classification; cultural services include cinema, live shows, museums, audiovisual subscriptions, and photo development.
observations.uncertainty: Shares are composition measures within cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure, not shares of all household consumption; 2024 is semi-definitive and 2025 provisional.
observations.subgroup: French households in the national accounts; no demographic or income breakdown is provided in this release.
observations.counterinterpretation: The service-share increase may reflect price changes, reopening and post-pandemic normalization, subscription accounting, or reclassification rather than more cultural participation or improved welfare.

observations.period: 2021-2025; books, press, and stationery within household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

denominator.unit: million euros of household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure in 2025; category composition denominator

books_press_stationery_share_2021.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

books_press_stationery_share_2022.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

books_press_stationery_share_2023.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

books_press_stationery_share_2024.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

books_press_stationery_share_2025.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

mechanism.value: Books, press, and stationery have lost composition share since 2021 even as cultural services gained share, indicating a shift in the paid cultural basket rather than a uniform expansion of every cultural category

observations.method: INSEE annual national accounts category shares and 2025 provisional values.
observations.uncertainty: The aggregate books/press/stationery category combines physical and potentially digital items under the classification and does not measure reading, attention, or cultural meaning.
observations.subgroup: French households in the national accounts; no income, age, education, or household-type breakdown in this release.
observations.counterinterpretation: Share decline can result from faster growth in other categories or relative price movements rather than a fall in book purchases or reading volume.

observations.period: 2021-2025; durable cultural and audiovisual/photo equipment within household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

denominator.unit: million euros of household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure in 2025; category composition denominator

other_durable_cultural_recreational_good.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure
percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

audiovisual_photographic_equipment_share.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure
percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure

services_plus_books_share_2025.unit: percent of cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure; cultural services plus books/press/stationery

mechanism.value: The paid cultural basket is becoming less equipment- and durable-good-heavy while services remain prominent, consistent with access shifting from ownership toward use, subscription, and venue/service purchase

observations.method: INSEE annual national accounts composition data using the revised COICOP classification; the combined 2025 service-plus-books figure is calculated from the published shares.
observations.uncertainty: The classification does not reveal device ownership, streaming quantity, household access, or whether services are consumed digitally or in person; the calculated combination is descriptive.
observations.subgroup: French households in the national accounts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Equipment-share decline may reflect durable replacement cycles, price changes, or reclassification, not a move away from owned cultural goods in every household.

related_sources.claim: INSEE table provides annual 2000-2025 cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure composition, category definitions, values, and provisional/semi-definitive status.
INSEE table and downloadable data identify the national-accounts source and revised COICOP classification.

boundary: This record adds French national-accounts evidence on the composition of household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure. It measures expenditure shares rather than participation, reach, frequency, quality, prices by category, income distribution, or cultural meaning; 2025 figures are provisional and the aggregate category is broader than culture alone.
